pages.text: A proton crossing a magnetic field circles, and how often it circles - $(thing)f = qB/2πm$() - does not depend on how fast it goes. Lawrence saw what that meant: put an RF voltage at that frequency across a gap, and the proton is kicked every half turn, spiralling out faster and faster in step.

Set the field B, then the RF to 15.25 MHz per tesla. At the edge, 0.75 m out, the beam has $(thing)E = (qBR)²/2m$(). But relativity: the faster it goes the heavier it is, its frequency drops, and over its hundreds of turns it slips out of phase. Past 90° the gap slows it instead. Tune a hair low to split the difference - the classical cyclotron runs out at about ten MeV.
Five MeV protons on iron make $(item)Cobalt-57$() (⁵⁷Fe(p,n)⁵⁷Co): the Pound-Rebka source, two at a time, without radium. Above 2.2 T the iron yoke saturates; more than 2 kW of beam melts the target.
